content: 1. Opnavir and Tisotumab Vedotin: Opnavir increases the levels of tisotumab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism in the liver and intestines. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is required. The active metabolite of tisotumab vedotin, MMAE, is a substrate of CYP3A4. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may elevate systemic exposure to unconjugated MMAE, increasing the risk of adverse effects. 2. Ritonavir and Tobramycin: Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of tobramycin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Lopinavir and Tofacitinib: Lopinavir increases the levels of tofacitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the tofacitinib dose to 5 mg once daily and monitor closely. 4. Ritonavir and Tolterodine: Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of tolterodine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Additionally, ritonavir affects CYP2D6 metabolism of tolterodine. Use caution and monitor closely. Lopinavir also increases tolterodine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 5. Tolvaptan and Ritonavir: Tolvaptan increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Conversely, ritonavir increases tolvaptan levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of significant interactions. 6. Topiramate and Ritonavir: Topiramate decreases ritonavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, topiramate reduces lopinavir levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Lopinavir and Topotecan: Lopinavir increases topotecan levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. For oral topotecan, avoid co-administration with P-gp inhibitors. The interaction with IV topotecan may be less severe but still clinically significant. 8. Ritonavir and Toremifene: Ritonavir increases toremifene levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Lopinavir has a similar effect on toremifene. Drugs that inhibit CYP3A4 may further inhibit toremifene metabolism. 9. Lopinavir and Trabectedin: Lopinavir increases trabectedin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used, administer it one week after trabectedin infusion and discontinue it the day before the next infusion. 10. Ritonavir and Tramadol: Ritonavir increases tramadol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This may necessitate a reduced tramadol dose or adjustment of dosing intervals. Increased risk of seizures and serotonin syndrome requires close monitoring. 11. Ritonavir and Trazodone: Ritonavir increases trazodone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, trazodone decreases ritonavir levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Ritonavir and Triamcinolone Acetonide: Ritonavir increases the levels of injectable triamcinolone acetonide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Lopinavir and Triazolam: Lopinavir increases triazolam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of severe adverse effects. 14. Lopinavir and Triclabendazole: Both lopinavir and triclabendazole prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Ritonavir and Trifluoperazine: Ritonavir increases trifluoperazine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 16. Lopinavir and Trimethoprim: Lopinavir increases trimethoprim levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 17. Ritonavir and Trimipramine: Ritonavir increases trimipramine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Lopinavir and Triptorelin: Triptorelin increases lopinavir toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug due to the risk of torsades de pointes. 19. Ritonavir and Tropisetron: Ritonavir increases tropisetron levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 20. Ritonavir and Tucatinib: Ritonavir increases tucatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Tucatinib also increases ritonavir levels. Avoid co-administration with CYP3A substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious toxicities. 21. Ritonavir and Ubrogepant: Ritonavir decreases ubrogepant levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose adjustment is recommended when co-administered with moderate or weak CYP3A4 inducers. 22. Ritonavir and Ulipristal: Ritonavir increases ulipristal levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 23. Ritonavir and Upadacitinib: Ritonavir increases upadacitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Ritonavir and Valbenazine: Ritonavir increases valbenazine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the valbenazine dose to 40 mg once daily when co-administered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 25. Ritonavir and Valsartan: Ritonavir increases valsartan levels by decreasing hepatic clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Ritonavir and Vandetanib: Ritonavir increases vandetanib toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 27. Ritonavir and Vardenafil: Ritonavir increases vardenafil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction may be necessary. 28. Ritonavir and Vemurafenib: Ritonavir increases vemurafenib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 29. Ritonavir and Venetoclax: Ritonavir increases venetoclax levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated during the initial ramp-up dosing phase. 30. Ritonavir and Venlafaxine: Ritonavir increases venlafaxine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Ritonavir and Verapamil: Ritonavir increases verapamil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 32. Ritonavir and Vilazodone: Ritonavir increases vilazodone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug.
